question: Could Ibn Turka's deference to the ancients be read as pure restoration, with history in decline?
proposition: On a perennialist model the wisdom tradition is static, its golden age at the dawn of time, and history can only decline from it; read this way Ibn Turka's ancients-first stance would be restoration alone.
reasoning: Melvin-Koushki names this model (philosophia perennis) as the European attempt to resolve the prisca-theologia paradox and says it is profoundly conservative (pdf p.339).
He sets it aside for Ibn Turka, citing his belief in recovery, tajdīd and upward development (pdf pp.340-341, 344).
The pages attribute no perennialist statement to Ibn Turka; the reading is listed here only as the rival the dissertation names.
